    36:     # pre_tasks are skipped unless tagged `always`, and `| mandatory` at the call
    37:     # sites fires only on UNDEFINED, not on empty. Without this, a rotation with an
    38:     # unfilled vault entry renders master_key: "" into LiteLLM's config and reports
    39:     # success — the same silently-passing guard as #238 itself.
    40:     #
    41:     # Scoped to this one variable rather than tagging the whole block, so tagged
    42:     # workflows that tolerate an empty optional secret keep working.
    43:     - name: Validate the LiteLLM master key (runs on tagged deploys too)
    44:       ansible.builtin.assert:
    45:         that:
    46:           - litellm_master_key is defined
    47:           - litellm_master_key | length > 0
    48:         fail_msg: |
    49:           litellm_master_key is unset or empty in ansible/vars/secrets.yml.
    50:           It authenticates the API, the interpret container, and the daily digest to
    51:           the LiteLLM router, and has no default by design (#238).
    52: 
    53:             python3 -c "import secrets; print('sk-' + secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"
    54:             ansible-vault edit ansible/vars/secrets.yml
    55:       tags: [always]
    56: 
    57:     # --- Deploy provenance (#151) ------------------------------------------
    58:     #
    59:     # Tagged `always` for exactly the reason the assert above is: a TAGGED deploy is
    60:     # when drift happens, and pre_tasks are skipped unless tagged. `make deploy
    61:     # TAGS=pipeline` is the common case, so a provenance marker that only appeared on
    62:     # full deploys would be absent precisely when it is needed.
    63:     #
    64:     # Records BRANCH and DIRTY, not just the SHA. On 2026-08-03 a `TAGS=pipeline`
    65:     # deploy ran from a clean `main` while the change under test (the qwen@15 arm)
    66:     # existed only on a feature branch. The host silently reverted to main's copy and
    67:     # the next eval would have run at the wrong depth for 50 minutes. A bare SHA would
    68:     # have looked perfectly healthy — main was clean and current. What was needed was
    69:     # the ability to ask "is THIS commit live?", which `make provenance` now answers.
    70:     # No `run_once` on these: the play targets a single host so they run once
    71:     # anyway, and ansible-lint's run-once[task] rule rejects it as
    72:     # strategy-dependent. The git reads are idempotent regardless.
    73:     - name: Read the deploying checkout's git HEAD
    74:       ansible.builtin.command:
    75:         cmd: git rev-parse HEAD
    76:         chdir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/.."
    77:       register: _deploy_sha
    78:       changed_when: false
    79:       delegate_to: localhost
    80:       become: false
    81:       tags: [always]
    82: 
    83:     - name: Read the deploying checkout's branch
    84:       ansible.builtin.command:
    85:         cmd: git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
    86:         chdir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/.."
    87:       register: _deploy_branch
    88:       changed_when: false
    89:       delegate_to: localhost
    90:       become: false
    91:       tags: [always]
    92: 
    93:     # Uncommitted changes mean the deployed bytes correspond to NO commit, so the SHA
    94:     # alone is a lie. Recorded rather than blocked: deploying a work-in-progress is a
    95:     # legitimate thing to do deliberately, and an unexplained hard failure here would
    96:     # just teach people to skip the check.
    97:     - name: Detect uncommitted changes in the deploying checkout
    98:       ansible.builtin.command:
    99:         cmd: git status --porcelain
   100:         chdir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/.."
   101:       register: _deploy_dirty
   102:       changed_when: false
   103:       delegate_to: localhost
   104:       become: false
   105:       tags: [always]
   106: 
   107:     - name: Look at the previous deploy's markers before overwriting them
   108:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   109:         path: "/opt/lamware/deploy-{{ item }}.json"
   110:       register: _prev_markers
   111:       loop: [started, provenance]
   112:       tags: [always]
   113: 
   114:     - name: Name the two previous markers
   115:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   116:         _prev_started: "{{ _prev_markers.results[0] }}"
   117:         _prev_completed: "{{ _prev_markers.results[1] }}"
   118:       tags: [always]
   119: 
   120:     - name: Ensure the provenance directory exists
   121:       ansible.builtin.file:
   122:         path: /opt/lamware
   123:         state: directory
   124:         mode: "0755"
   125:       tags: [always]
   126: 
   127:     # STARTED, not deployed. This runs before a single role, so it records what
   128:     # the deploy INTENDED. A play that aborts mid-way leaves this behind and
   129:     # nothing else — which is how a failed deploy on 2026-09-01 reported the
   130:     # full tag list while `grep -c single_shot_backend runner.py` returned 0 on
   131:     # the host (#515). The completed marker is written in post_tasks, where it
   132:     # can only exist if every role ran.
   133:     - name: Write the deploy STARTED marker
   134:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   135:         dest: /opt/lamware/deploy-started.json
   136:         mode: "0644"
   137:         content: |
   138:           {{
   139:             {
   140:               "sha": _deploy_sha.stdout,
   141:               "branch": _deploy_branch.stdout,
   142:               "dirty": (_deploy_dirty.stdout | length) > 0,
   143:               "dirty_files": (_deploy_dirty.stdout_lines | default([]))[:20],
   144:               "tags": (ansible_run_tags | default(["all"])),
   145:               "deployed_at": (ansible_date_time.iso8601 | default("unknown")),
   146:               "deployed_by": (lookup("env", "USER") | default("unknown", true)),
   147:             } | to_nice_json
   148:           }}
   149:       tags: [always]
   150: 
   151:     - name: Warn when the previous deploy never finished
   152:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   153:         msg: >-
   154:           PREVIOUS DEPLOY DID NOT COMPLETE — a started marker exists with no
   155:           matching completed one, so the host is in whatever state that play
   156:           left it. Treat `make provenance` as unverified until this deploy ends.
   157:       when:
   158:         - _prev_started.stat.exists
   159:         - (not _prev_completed.stat.exists)
   160:           or (_prev_started.stat.mtime > _prev_completed.stat.mtime)
   161:       tags: [always]
   162: 
   163:     - name: Report what is being deployed
   164:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   165:         msg: >-
   166:           Deploying {{ _deploy_sha.stdout[:12] }} ({{ _deploy_branch.stdout }}){{
   167:           ' [DIRTY — deployed bytes match no commit]' if (_deploy_dirty.stdout | length) > 0 else '' }}
   168:           tags={{ ansible_run_tags | default(['all']) | join(',') }}
   169:       tags: [always]
   170: 
   171:   roles:

    78: # Configure application stacks based on OpenTofu infrastructure
    79: 
    80: # =============================================================================
    81: # Phase 0-secrets: OpenBao resource-domain secrets pre-fetch
    82: # Reads each resource-domain's KV subtree (its own least-privilege AppRole)
    83: # into a per-domain `bao_<domain>_secrets` fact so every consumer role can
    84: # resolve its secrets bao-first with an env fallback. Runs once on the
    85: # controller and publishes to the union of every domain's consuming groups;
    86: # each domain SKIPS CLEANLY when BAO_ADDR or that domain's own role_id/
    87: # secret_id envs are unset.
    88: # =============================================================================

    92:     ai_orchestration_group:n8n_group:
    93:     cribl_stream_group:cribl_edge:
    94:     object_storage_group:

    96:     postgres_group:postgres_ai_group:hindsight_group:nautobot_group:zammad_group:vikunja_group:
    97:     immich_group:homarr_group:authelia_group:grafana_group

   100:   # converge (--tags zammad, --tags nautobot, ...) MUST still run this play —
   101:   # under the old `openbao_secrets, ai` tags a tagged converge skipped the
   102:   # fetch and templated empty passwords (zammad database.yml, 2026-07-16).
   103:   # The role still skips cleanly when BAO_ADDR / a domain's AppRole envs are
   104:   # unset, so `always` costs nothing in env-less runs.
   105:   tags:
   106:     - always
   107:   # Wrapped in block/rescue for play-level failure isolation (issue #672): a
   108:   # hard failure on one host in this large combined-group play (e.g. an
   109:   # undefined var) would otherwise be 100% of that host's "batch" and abort
   110:   # every remaining play in site.yml, not just this one. See
   111:   # tasks/record_isolated_failure.yml for the mechanism.
   112:   tasks:
   113:     - name: Converge OpenBao secrets pre-fetch (isolated — failure does not abort downstream plays)
   114:       block:
   115:         - name: Fetch each resource-domain's KV subtree via its own AppRole
   116:           ansible.builtin.include_role:
   117:             name: openbao_secrets
   118: 
   119:         # Publish each domain's shared, un-prefixed fact at the playbook layer
   120:         # (like tofu_data in load_tofu.yml). openbao_secrets_by_domain was
   121:         # computed once on the delegated controller; a domain that was skipped
   122:         # (BAO_ADDR or that domain's creds unset) is simply absent from the dict,
   123:         # so `default({})` covers it the same as a host outside this play.
   124:         - name: Publish each domain's merged secrets to every host in this play
   125:           ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   126:             bao_observability_secrets: "{{ openbao_secrets_by_domain['observability'] | default({}) }}"
   127:             bao_local_cloud_secrets: "{{ openbao_secrets_by_domain['local-cloud'] | default({}) }}"
   128:             bao_monitoring_secrets: "{{ openbao_secrets_by_domain['monitoring'] | default({}) }}"
   129:             bao_media_secrets: "{{ openbao_secrets_by_domain['media'] | default({}) }}"
   130:             bao_local_llm_secrets: "{{ openbao_secrets_by_domain['local-llm'] | default({}) }}"
   131:             bao_apps_secrets: "{{ openbao_secrets_by_domain['apps'] | default({}) }}"
   132:           vars:
   133:             openbao_secrets_by_domain: "{{ hostvars['localhost'].openbao_secrets_by_domain | default({}) }}"
   134:           no_log: true
   135:       rescue:
   136:         - name: Record isolated failure and continue
   137:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: ../tasks/record_isolated_failure.yml
   138:           vars:
   139:             _isolated_play_name: openbao-secrets-prefetch

     4:   become: true

    13:     # (inventory/group_vars/all.yml), never reconstructed here.

    27:         fail_msg: >-
    28:           SPLUNK_PASSWORD environment variable must be set.
    29:           Run with doppler run --
    30:         quiet: true
    31: 
    32:     - name: Check netflow UDP port is listening
    33:       ansible.builtin.shell:
    34:         cmd: |
    35:           set -o pipefail
    36:           ss -ulnp | grep ':{{ constants.netflow_ports.unifi }}'
    37:         executable: /bin/bash
    38:       register: netflow_port_check
    39:       failed_when: netflow_port_check.rc != 0
    40:       changed_when: false
    41: 
    42:     - name: Generate unique sentinel port for NetFlow test correlation
    43:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    44:         netflow_sentinel_port: "{{ 40000 + (ansible_date_time.epoch | int % 25000) }}"
    45: 
    46:     - name: Send minimal NetFlow v5 test packet
    47:       ansible.builtin.shell:
    48:         cmd: |
    49:           python3 -c "
    50:           import socket, struct, time
    51: 
    52:           # NetFlow v5 header: version=5, count=1, uptime=0
    53:           # epoch, nanosec, flow_seq=1, engine=0, sampling=0
    54:           epoch = int(time.time())
    55:           header = struct.pack('!HHIIIIBBH',
    56:               5,       # version
    57:               1,       # count (1 flow record)
    58:               0,       # sys_uptime_ms
    59:               epoch,   # unix_secs
    60:               0,       # unix_nsecs
    61:               1,       # flow_sequence
    62:               0,       # engine_type + engine_id (packed as one byte each below)
    63:               0,       # engine_id
    64:               0        # sampling_interval
    65:           )
    66: 
    67:           # NetFlow v5 flow record (48 bytes): minimal valid record
    68:           # Uses sentinel src_port for test correlation in Splunk
    69:           record = struct.pack('!IIIHHIIIIHHBBBBHHBBH',
    70:               0x0A000001,  # src_addr 10.0.0.1
    71:               0x0A000002,  # dst_addr 10.0.0.2
    72:               0,           # next_hop
    73:               0,           # snmp_input
    74:               0,           # snmp_output
    75:               1,           # packets
    76:               64,          # octets
    77:               0,           # first_switched
    78:               0,           # last_switched
    79:               {{ netflow_sentinel_port }},  # src_port (sentinel)
    80:               80,          # dst_port
    81:               0,           # pad1
    82:               6,           # tcp_flags
    83:               6,           # protocol (TCP)
    84:               0,           # tos
    85:               0,           # src_as
    86:               0,           # dst_as
    87:               0,           # src_mask
    88:               0,           # dst_mask
    89:               0            # pad2
    90:           )
    91: 
    92:           sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
    93:           sock.sendto(header + record, ('127.0.0.1', {{ constants.netflow_ports.unifi }}))
    94:           sock.close()
    95:           print('NetFlow v5 test packet sent with sentinel src_port={{ netflow_sentinel_port }}')
    96:           "
    97:         executable: /bin/bash
    98:       changed_when: false
    99: 
   100:     - name: Wait for NetFlow event to propagate through pipeline
   101:       ansible.builtin.pause:
   102:         seconds: 10
   103:         prompt: >-
   104:           Waiting for NetFlow test event to propagate through Cribl Stream to Splunk...
   105: 
   106:     # Pipeline latency assertion: poll up to 120 seconds (retries: 12, delay: 10)
   107:     # The loop fails the play if the event does not appear within 120 seconds.
   108:     - name: Query Splunk for NetFlow event in netflow index (pipeline latency assertion, 120s timeout)
   109:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   110:         url: "{{ splunk_mgmt_base_url }}/services/search/jobs"
   111:         method: POST
   112:         user: "{{ splunk_user }}"
   113:         password: "{{ splunk_password }}"
   114:         force_basic_auth: true
   115:         validate_certs: false
   116:         body_format: form-urlencoded
   117:         body:
   118:           # Cribl's netflow input emits camelCase srcPort (preserved by
   119:           # Splunk's JSON auto-extraction) — src_port never matches.
   120:           search: 'search index=netflow earliest=-5m srcPort={{ netflow_sentinel_port }} | head 1'
   121:           output_mode: json
   122:           exec_mode: oneshot
   123:       register: splunk_netflow_result
   124:       retries: 12
   125:       delay: 10
   126:       until: >-
   127:         splunk_netflow_result.status == 200 and
   128:         (splunk_netflow_result.json.results | default([]) | length > 0)
   129:       failed_when: >-
   130:         splunk_netflow_result.status != 200 or
   131:         (splunk_netflow_result.json.results | default([]) | length == 0)
   132: 
   133:     - name: Display NetFlow validation result
   134:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   135:         msg: |
   136:           === NETFLOW VALIDATION PASSED ===
   137:           NetFlow port {{ constants.netflow_ports.unifi }} UDP is listening
   138:           {{ netflow_port_check.stdout }}
   139:           NetFlow v5 test packet sent and event found in Splunk
   140:           Splunk host: {{ splunk_mgmt_base_url }}
   141:           Search results (index=netflow): {{ splunk_netflow_result.json.results | length }} event(s) found
   142:           Full path verified: NetFlow source -> Cribl Stream LXC -> Splunk HEC -> Splunk Index (netflow)

    83:     # here: play vars OUTRANK group_vars, so any ghapp_* left in this vars: block

   136:             owner: root
   137:             group: root
   138:             mode: "0644"
   139:             content: |
   140:               # Loaded for docker-ce's iptables/NAT bridge networking (see
   141:               # playbooks/devenv/bootstrap.yml). These live in
   142:               # kernel-modules-extra, absent from the CentOS Stream 10 golden image.
   143:               xt_addrtype
   144:               iptable_nat
   145:               br_netfilter

   147:         - name: Load the netfilter modules now

   150:             state: present
   151:           loop:
   152:             - xt_addrtype
   153:             - iptable_nat
   154:             - br_netfilter

   156:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
   157:     # One-shot Docker data-root migration (igou-inventory#373). Only runs
   158:     # when a daemon is already up with a root dir other than
   159:     # docker_data_root: stop the devcontainer unit (its ExecStop removes
   160:     # the container, and the unit is started again at the end of this play),
   161:     # stop the daemon, copy the store, and park the old tree as
   162:     # /var/lib/docker.migrated. The docker role then renders daemon.json

   164:     # the root dir and delete the parked tree. Fresh hosts (no daemon yet)
   165:     # skip straight to the role, which creates the store in place.
   166:     # ------------------------------------------------------------------

   168:       ansible.builtin.command:

   170:       register: devenv_docker_root
   171:       changed_when: false
   172:       failed_when: false
   173:       become: true
   174: 
   175:     - name: Migrate the Docker store to {{ docker_data_root }}
   176:       become: true
   177:       when:
   178:         - devenv_docker_root.rc == 0
   179:         - devenv_docker_root.stdout | trim != docker_data_root

    36:         - name: Clear stale firewall rules
    37:           ansible.builtin.shell:
    38:             executable: /bin/bash
    39:             cmd: |
    40:               set -e
    41:               IFS=$'\n'
    42: 
    43:               current_rules=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --get-all-rules | grep "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_" || true)
    44:               for rule in $current_rules; do
    45:                 rule_name=$(echo "$rule" | awk '{print $NF}' | sed 's/{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_//')
    46:                 if ! echo "{{ ftp_firewall_rules | map(attribute='name') | list }}" | grep -q "'$rule_name'"; then
    47:                   # `$rule` cannot be passed directly to remove the rule because it will be treated as a
    48:                   # single argument, so split it into an array to pass each part as a separate argument
    49:                   IFS=' ' read -r -a rule_parts <<< "$rule"
    50:                   firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --remove-rule "${rule_parts[@]}"
    51:                   echo "Rule removed: '$rule_name'"
    52:                 fi
    53:               done
    54:           register: ftp_firewall_rules_cleanup
    55:           changed_when: "'Rule removed' in ftp_firewall_rules_cleanup.stdout"
    56: 
    57:         - name: Deploy firewall rules
    58:           ansible.builtin.shell:
    59:             executable: /bin/bash
    60:             cmd: |
    61:               set -e
    62: 
    63:               existing_rule=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --get-all-rules | grep "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_{{ item.name }}$" || true)
    64:               if [[ -n "$existing_rule" ]]; then
    65:                 firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --remove-rule $existing_rule

    67: 
    68:               firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --add-rule {{ item.rule }} -m comment --comment "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_{{ item.name }}"
    69:               new_rule=$(firewall-cmd --permanent --direct --get-all-rules | grep "{{ ftp_firewall_rules_tag }}_{{ item.name }}$")

    71:               if [[ "$new_rule" != "$existing_rule" ]]; then
    72:                 echo "Rule changed: '{{ item.name }}'"
    73:               fi

    75:           loop_control:
    76:             label: "{{ item.name }}"

    78:           changed_when: "'Rule changed' in ftp_firewall_rules_deploy.stdout"
